Ford just told the UK government that new rules are “unworkable”. These rules, called the ZEV mandate, say that a growing figure of the cars each company sells must be electric. The twist is that in 2022, Ford was part of the group strongly supporting these rules—and even asked for tougher targets—because it thought that would help push investment and make charging stations grow, so the whole operation of switching to electric would bear fruit faster.  

  
female executives at Ford did warn that the rules should be checked again if market conditions changed, and that is what they are pointing to now. Demand for electric cars is not growing as fast as it was, so Ford is finding it harder to sell as many as the rules require. During Covid, when money was cheaper to borrow, carmakers could basically sing with relief because every car they built was snapped up; now, with higher costs and slower sales, the situation looks very different.  

  
P.P.S The passage is mainly saying that Ford has done a U-turn: it once pushed for stricter electric-car rules, but now that sales are tougher, it is criticising the same policy it helped promote, showing how quickly business positions can change when markets shift. Any other questions?
